response.title: can a power station be used as a ups
response.answer:
Yes, a portable power station can be used as a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply), but not every power station is suitable for this purpose.

The key difference is how quickly it switches from grid power to battery power when an outage occurs.

Power station vs. traditional UPS

Feature

	

Portable power station

	

Traditional UPS




Backup power

	

Yes

	

Yes




Automatic switchover

	

Model-dependent

	

Yes




Transfer time

	

Typically 0–30 ms on UPS-capable models

	

Typically 0–10 ms




Battery capacity

	

Often 500–4,000+ Wh

	

Often 100–1,000 Wh




Runtime

	

Usually longer

	

Usually shorter




Voltage regulation

	

Model-dependent

	

Often included




Designed for 24/7 UPS use

	

Not always

	

Yes

Three things to check

1. Transfer time (most important)

When grid power fails, some power stations briefly interrupt their AC output before switching to battery.

0 ms: Ideal for sensitive electronics.

Under 10 ms: Usually suitable for computers, networking equipment, and NAS devices.

10–20 ms: May work, but some computers could restart.

Over 20 ms: Generally not recommended for sensitive equipment.

A power station advertising "UPS mode" doesn't necessarily provide zero-interruption power.

2. Pass-through charging

The power station needs to support simultaneous AC input and AC output.

The typical setup is:

Wall outlet (AC power)

Power station

Pass-through / UPS mode

Computer / NAS / Router

3. Continuous operation

Some power stations aren't designed to remain plugged in and supply power 24/7.

Check for:

Explicit manufacturer support for UPS operation.

Battery management that prevents excessive cycling.

Sufficient continuous AC output wattage.

Pure sine wave AC output.

Overload and thermal protection.

My recommendation

If you're protecting a desktop PC, server, or NAS, a traditional UPS is generally the safer choice because it is specifically designed for uninterrupted power.

If you want several hours of backup runtime, a power station with a properly implemented UPS mode can be a better option.

One question: What are you planning to power with it? A desktop PC, NAS/server, router, or something else?

The answer matters because a 20 ms transfer time may be perfectly acceptable for one device but cause another to reboot.
